thread:
Kai Nakamura: quick pulse-check: RFC follow-up idea 7: define compact runtime tokens that reference authority artifacts (role ids, bundle version) instead of embedding full RBAC. goal: reduce gateway path size and CPU.
Sana Reddy: this aligns w/ earlier notes. we should pick a canonical compact schema and migration strategy.
Diego Alvarez: checklist: 1) token schema, 2) broker adapter for legacy keys, 3) gateway cache behavior + eviction, 4) offline bundle format for Private installs.
Helena Park: token schema proposal (ultra compact):
```
{iss:k, sub:svc:payments:42, rid:12345, bv:20260321T10, ds:55a3, exp:1799913600}
```
where rid is registry id mapping to role membership, bv is bundle version, ds optional dataset hash. minimal keys, no arrays.
Kai Nakamura: love it. a couple tradeoffs: rid resolution freshness vs revocation window. need clear semantics for eventual consistency.
Sana Reddy: revocation model: update registry -> bundles include tombstones -> gateways deny after bundle refresh or on explicit revocation push. document worst-case TTL exposure.
Diego Alvarez: migration ops: broker accepts legacy API key and returns ephemeral token (TTL 5-15m). we audit every exchange. customers keep old key but exposure minimized.
Helena Park: offline bundles: compressed proto that contains numeric role defs, route ACLs, paramized predicates (e.g., dataset hash allowlist). signed by control plane; gateways verify signature on ingest.
Kai Nakamura: perf: signature verify is heavy per-token. gateway should maintain LRU of verified token ids and only reverify on new tokens or key rotation. add session cache metrics.
Sana Reddy: role-id registry: central mapping service exposing delta stream. gateways subscribe to deltas to pre-warm caches. delta entries: add/remove/mutate membership for rid.
Diego Alvarez: audit: gateways emit decision records asynchronously with token_id, rid, bv, decision, and reason. private installs can opt to keep logs local or ship to central collector.
Helena Park: failure modes: stale bundle -> gateway can either fail-closed or fallback to remote policy eval. prefer fail-closed for sensitive routes, allow fallback for low-risk ones. document per-route policy.
auth-bot: added runbook todo "compact-token-rfc-update" https://redwood.internal/runbooks/compact-token-rfc
Kai Nakamura: next steps: Sana write token schema + RFC appendix, Diego prototype broker adapter and audit events, Helena draft bundle proto + signing example, I'll mock perf sim for session cache. reconvene Thu 9am to finalize RFC.
Sana Reddy: will post a strawman schema by EOD.
Diego Alvarez: will have a tiny adapter prototype and logs sample by Wed.
Helena Park: bundle proto draft tomorrow.
Kai Nakamura: thanks team. aim is a compact runtime token + robust bundle/delta model so we can serve Hosted + Dedicated + Private without sacrificing latency or control.
